PAPERS.short: Xiao air pollution kidney disease mortality subtypes China case-crossover 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution exposure and death from different subtypes of kidney diseases: A nationwide, individual-level, case-crossover study in China.
PAPERS.pm: Modelled daily PM2.5 and PM2.5-10 at residential address, with O3 and NO2
PAPERS.endpoint: Kidney disease mortality and subtypes (renal failure, glomerular, tubulointerstitial, urolithiasis)
PAPERS.affil: Fudan University, China; Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, China
PAPERS.n: 466,543 kidney deaths, China 2013-2019, time-stratified case-crossover with conditional logistic regression. Per IQR: PM2.5 lag 0-2 OR 1.0195 (1.0122-1.0269); coarse PM2.5-10 lag 0-3 OR 1.0240 (1.0158-1.0323); O3 +2.05% (1.05-3.07); NO2 lag 0-3 +3.62% (2.47-4.78). Renal failure and glomerular deaths responded to all four pollutants; tubulointerstitial deaths to O3 only; urolithiasis null. Limitation: the abstract does not give the IQR widths, so 'NO2 strongest' is not a per-mass comparison, the lag differs by pollutant, and renal failure on a death certificate is often a proximate cause. Relevance: moderate - coarse-mode signal comparable to PM2.5 per IQR, in a size fraction low-cost optical sensors undercount.

PAPERS.short: Calderon-Garciduenas ferrimagnetic nanoparticles olfactory bulb cortex Mexico City children 2026
PAPERS.title: The olfactory bulb, prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex are early pediatric targets for anthropogenic magnetic nanoparticles and their motion behavior under electromagnetic fields.
PAPERS.pm: Ferrimagnetic nanoparticles in brain tissue by magnetophoresis, TEM and EDX
PAPERS.endpoint: Presence, composition and field-induced motion of magnetic nanoparticles in brain
PAPERS.affil: University of Montana, United States; Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, Mexico
PAPERS.n: 48 brain samples (olfactory bulb, anterior cingulate, prefrontal cortex) from 12 children (8.5 +/- 7.6 y) and 16 adults (39.2 +/- 19.6 y), Metropolitan Mexico City. Magnetophoresis at 25-1,000 mT AC showed small displacements and significant vector-direction variation; TEM and EDX located ferrimagnetic nanoparticles. No effect size. Limitation: autopsy convenience series with no comparison population or exposure measure in the abstract, so 'early pediatric targets' and the neural-damage risk are inferred, not tested; particle attribution to anthropogenic sources is not apportioned here. Relevance: low for sensing - mass-calibrated optical nodes are blind to this metallic ultrafine fraction, which is the actual argument for co-located number or magnetic measurements.

PAPERS.short: Aretz sick leave long-term fine particulate German health claims 13-year 2026
PAPERS.title: Assessing the health and economic burden of sick leave associated with long-term fine particulate matter exposure: a 13-year analysis using German health claims data
PAPERS.pm: Long-term fine PM (exposure source not available)
PAPERS.endpoint: Sick leave and economic burden (per title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit, no abstract in Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar; no finding asserted. The title describes a 13-year analysis of German health claims linking long-term fine PM to sick leave and its economic burden. Limitation: exposure source, increment, cohort size and estimate are all unknown until the abstract deposits. Relevance: to be assessed - claims-linked sick leave is a working-age endpoint rarely paired with PM, and this is the first record to retry on the next weekly abstract sweep.

PAPERS.short: Nie personal air purification device multi-scale modelling fan speed occupant exposure 2026
PAPERS.title: Multi-scale modeling and fan speed optimization of a personal air-purification device for occupant exposure control in polluted indoor environments
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit, no abstract in Crossref or Semantic Scholar; no finding asserted. The title describes multi-scale modelling and fan-speed optimisation of a personal air-purification device. Limitation: the title does not confirm particulate matter as the pollutant, and no performance figures, validation or occupant data are available. Relevance: to be assessed - breathing-zone control is where stationary sensors misstate exposure; retain only if the abstract confirms a PM target and measured validation.

PAPERS.short: Alli ambient air pollution blood pressure schoolchildren Accra LUR 2026
PAPERS.title: Urban ambient air pollution and blood pressure in schoolchildren in Accra, Ghana
PAPERS.pm: Home and school PM2.5, BC, NO2 from spatiotemporal LUR (146 measurement sites)
PAPERS.endpoint: Systolic and diastolic BP; elevated BP
PAPERS.affil: University of Massachusetts Amherst, United States; University of Massachusetts Amherst, United States
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (entry date 4 Jun 2026; Amass). 919 children aged 7-14 in 90 schools; one-third with elevated BP. Per 10 units home exposure: SBP PM2.5 -0.70 mmHg (-3.34 to 1.94), BC -4.61 (-9.59 to 0.37); DBP PM2.5 -0.83 (-2.93 to 1.28), BC -4.35 (-8.19 to -0.50); elevated BP PM2.5 OR 0.75 (0.39-1.41). Exposures ran 5-8 times the WHO annual PM2.5 guideline. Limitation: cross-sectional, and inverse associations in a high-exposure city suggest residual confounding by socioeconomic or adiposity patterning; the upper bound does not exclude a moderate SBP rise. Relevance: high - the LUR rests on a 146-site campaign in sub-Saharan Africa, the design a low-cost network could sustain.

PAPERS.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
PAPERS.short: Hess low-level PM2.5 mortality Native American Medicare geographic attenuation 2026
PAPERS.title: Untangling Impacts of Socioeconomic Position, Chronic Disease, and Low-Level PM2.5 Exposure on Mortality Among Native American Medicare Beneficiaries
PAPERS.pm: Long-term low-level PM2.5 (lowest-decile zip codes; exposure source not stated)
PAPERS.affil: Hess Epidemiology Services, United States; University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, United States
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (entry date 4 May 2026; Amass). Case-control within 1,713,399 traditional Medicare beneficiaries in the lowest PM2.5 decile, 2015-2016, with PCA summaries of area SEP and chronic disease. Fully adjusted OR per ug/m3: Native American 1.12 (1.06-1.18), non-Native American 1.01 (1.001-1.02). Sequential adjustment attributed most attenuation in Native American beneficiaries to state-level clustering, less to SEP and disease. Limitation: the abstract gives no pre-adjustment coefficient, zip-level exposure over a narrow range makes a per-ug/m3 slope fragile, and state effects may absorb real exposure contrast. Relevance: moderate - low-level gradients are where sparse monitoring error is largest.

PAPERS.short: Ruvuna ambient PM2.5 NO2 plasma proteomics SPIROMICS SomaScan congress 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations of ambient air pollution and protein expression among individuals from the Subpopulations and intermediate outcome measures in COPD study (SPIROMICS)
PAPERS.pm: Modelled prior-year average PM2.5 and NO2
PAPERS.n: BACKFILL (Crossref deposit 29 Oct 2026; Amass; no PMID). ERS congress abstract. SPIROMICS tobacco-exposed cohort, n=1,627 for PM2.5 and n=1,618 for NO2; SomaScan 7k against modelled prior-year exposure, adjusted for site, COPD status, smoking, BMI, occupation, income and deprivation. 860 proteins associated with PM2.5 at FDR<0.05, none with NO2; enrichment in vascular remodelling, insulin signalling and inflammation. Limitation: abstract only, no effect sizes or replication, cross-sectional, and a one-pollutant-sided result may partly reflect exposure-model quality or spatial confounding. Relevance: low - no sensing element, but the proteomic contrast depends on exposure accuracy.
